claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr exhibits unusual stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior.
Temperature-induced elemental segregation and nano-precipitate formation govern this unusual behavior.
Differential thermal expansion between precipitates or segregated regions and the matrix generates localized residual stresses.
The localized residual stresses alter dislocation mobility.
Residual-stress-mediated changes in dislocation mobility cause temperature-dependent creep, deformation hardening, and anomalous elastic-modulus behavior.
Rapid quenching produces a homogeneous, single-phase BCC HfNbTaTiZr baseline.
Rapid quenching minimizes initial elemental segregation and precipitate formation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at 600–800 °C will promote elemental segregation and nano-precipitate formation.
The thermally induced segregated regions will be enriched particularly in Ta, Hf, or Zr.
Intermediate-temperature heat treatment can cause initially single-phase RHEAs to phase-separate and form precipitates around 700–800 °C.
Residual stresses increase dislocation pinning and lattice friction.
Stable nano-precipitate formation during aging strengthens or refines the proposed residual-stress and pinning effects.
Aged, segregated or precipitate-containing HfNbTaTiZr will have a lower steady-state creep rate at 1250 °C than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Aged HfNbTaTiZr will have higher microhardness after cold rolling than the rapidly quenched baseline because of enhanced dislocation pinning.
Aging-induced segregation or precipitation will modify the elastic-modulus temperature dependence between 293 and 1100 K, potentially reducing its temperature sensitivity.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to creep at temperatures of at least 1000 °C and to elastic behavior between 293 and 1100 K.
The proposed mechanism may cease to govern if oxidation, impurity effects, or extensive phase separation dominate the microstructure.
